questions.question: How many Grand Slam tournaments are played in a year in tennis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• The four annual tennis tournaments, also known as **majors**, are collectively called the **Grand Slam. **
 
• The** ITF—the International Tennis Federation—**operates the Grand Slam.
 
• The Grand Slam tournaments consist of the **mid-January Australian Open, the late May French Open or Roland Garros, the Wimbledon at the end of June and the US Open at the end of August.**
 
• The **four Grand Slam tennis tournaments** are played over the course of** 2 weeks. **
 
• The oldest is **Wimbledon Tennis, established in 1877,** then comes the **US Open in 1881 followed by the French Open in 1891, and the last is Australian Open in 1905.**
 
• The Australian tennis and US tournaments are played on hard courts,** the French Open on clay courts, and the Wimbledon on grass courts.**
 
• Before 1924-1925, the** French Open tournament** was not considered a Grand Slam.
 
• Together, the four majors are considered a "**boxed set**" of Grand Slam tournaments in all three disciplines (singles, doubles, and mixed doubles).
 
• During the course of a lifetime, winning all four majors is considered a** career Grand Slam.**
 
• It is considered a **non-calendar year Grand Slam** to win the four majors in consecutive events, but not in the same year.

questions.question: Where was the first Durand Cup, India’s oldest football tournament, held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shimla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Durand Cup is the oldest football tournament in India and was first held in 1888.
 
• The tournament was named after Mortimer Durand, who was the Foreign Secretary in charge of India at that time.
 
• The inaugural tournament was held in Shimla, which served as the summer capital of British India.
 
• Initially, the tournament was started as a football competition for British troops stationed in India but later it was opened to civilians as well.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Durand Cup**

 
 
• The Durand Cup is named after Sir Mortimer Durand, who was the Foreign Secretary of British India from 1884 to 1894.
 
• It is one of the oldest football competitions in the world and the oldest in Asia.
 
• The tournament is organized annually and has seen participation from top football clubs in India.
 
• Winners of the Durand Cup are awarded three trophies: the President's Cup (added in 1956), the Durand Cup (the original trophy), and the Shimla Trophy (added in 1904).
 
 
 
• **Football in India**
 
 
• Football is one of the most popular sports in India, especially in states like West Bengal, Goa, Kerala, and the northeastern states.
 
• The All India Football Federation (AIFF) is the governing body for football in India.
 
• The Indian Super League (ISL) and I-League are the top professional football leagues in the country.
 
• India has a rich history in football, with clubs like Mohun Bagan and East Bengal having a storied legacy.

questions.question: Which of the following states topped the medals tally in the Northeast Olympic Games 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipur**__.

• **Manipur** secured the top spot in the **Northeast Olympic Games** for the **second consecutive time**, clinching a **total of 237 medals**, with an impressive tally of 85 golds. 
 
• **Assam **closely followed in second place, accumulating 201 medals, including 81 golds. 
 
• The event, featuring athletes from eight states in the northeast region, took place on November 10. 
 
• This victory marks Manipur's continued dominance in the Games, building upon their previous success when they hosted the inaugural edition in October 2018 and topped the medal tally with 80 golds. 
 
• Renowned for producing Olympic medalists like boxer MC Mary Kom and weightlifter Mirabai Chanu, Manipur further solidified its position by securing an additional 17 medals, including seven golds, on the final day of competition.

• This performance marked a significant improvement for Meghalaya compared to their sixth-place finish in the first edition, where they secured only 39 medals. 
 
• Meanwhile, as preparations for the** "Manipur Olympic Games 2022" **were underway, Manipur's Chief Minister Nongthombam Biren Singh unveiled the official mascot of the event, named Nongin after the state bird of Manipur, Mrs. Hume's pheasant. 
 
• Recognizing the importance of preserving this bird species and raising public awareness in Manipur, the Government of Manipur, led by Chief Minister Biren, officially adopted Nongin as the mascot for the sports event.
